amendments.normalized_body: Fix dimensional mismatch in plant substrate limitation factors at plant_growth.rs:60-61. `substrate_n_factor = half_saturation(substrate_n, plant_half_saturation_n_mg_n_per_l)` passes raw mg totals from `total_substrate_n()` (e.g. 40 mg) against a concentration-based half-saturation constant (e.g. 0.4 mg/L after legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l divides by 20). This makes `half_saturation(40, 0.4) ≈ 0.99`, rendering substrate limitation essentially non-functional regardless of actual nutrient depletion. Same issue for substrate_p_factor. Either (a) convert substrate totals to a per-area or per-volume density before passing to half_saturation, or (b) use the original total-based half-saturation constant for the substrate compartment while reserving the concentration-based constant for water-column terms.

Add a test for plant substrate limitation that verifies substrate depletion actually reduces the limitation factor. The existing test `plant_water_column_limitation_is_volume_invariant_at_fixed_concentration` explicitly zeroes out substrate bias (`substrate_uptake_bias: Some(0.0)`) and clears substrate layers, so it cannot catch the dimensional mismatch in the substrate half-saturation path. A test with nonzero substrate bias and varying substrate nutrient levels would catch this class of bug.

`crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:48-50` and `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:76-82` migrate schema-v2 saves by rescaling dissolved totals onto net water volume, but they never reseed `state.stability_tracker` afterward. If an older save omits that field, serde falls back to `StabilityTracker::default` (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:204-224`), so the first daily `update_stability_tracker` run will compare the loaded chemistry against hard-coded defaults instead of the migrated water state and can inject a bogus instability spike into shrimp health/mortality. Reseed the tracker after migration/loading with the migrated `state.water` and `state.water_volume_l()`.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:8-13` converts the plant half-saturation parameters to mg/L, but `crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:60-61` then applies those mg/L constants to `substrate_n`/`substrate_p`, and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:356-369` shows those substrate values are still raw mg totals. That unit mismatch makes substrate limitation almost always saturate whenever the bed has any meaningful charge, and it still scales with absolute substrate mass instead of a normalized compartment quantity. Root-feeding growth is therefore no longer volume/footprint invariant in the substrate path. Either keep the substrate side on the legacy total-based constants for now or add a normalized substrate helper before using the new mg/L thresholds there.
